Graft one key onto a result of another

Source: R/prune.R
mergeKeys.Rd

Joins two keys end to end: the lead of key that ended in the taxon at now leads to the first couplet of subkey. Use it to put a key to the genera of one family under a key to families, or a regional key under a general one.

Usage

mergeKeys(key, subkey, at, labels = c("renumber", "prefix"), prefix = NULL)

Arguments

key

A dimoose key.

subkey

The dimoose key to graft onto it.

at

The result of key that subkey continues from: its whole label, the scientific name in its parentheses or the common name before them (case does not matter). It is an error if no result, or more than one, has that name; a shared result is named in full ("A / B").

labels

How to keep couplet names unique. "renumber" numbers the couplets of the merged key 1, 2, 3, ... in reading order, so the subkey's couplets follow the lead they hang from. "prefix" keeps key's couplet names and puts prefix in front of the subkey's.

prefix

Text put in front of the subkey's couplet names with labels = "prefix"; by default the scientific name of at and a full stop ("Salicaceae.1").

Value

A dimoose key.

Details

The leads of the two keys are put in one table (a column that only one of them has is left blank for the other), and so are their metadata, embedded images, taxa and features. key's title is kept; subkey's citation is added to key's. If at is the result of several leads, they all lead to the subkey. An embedded image or a feature that the two keys both have under one id, with different contents, is kept apart by giving the subkey's a new id (_2 is added), with a warning for a feature.

See also

pruneKey()

Examples

families <- keyFromLeads(data.frame(
  Statement = c("1", "1"), Choice = c("a", "b"),
  Character = c("Fruit an acorn", "Fruit a capsule releasing cottony seeds"),
  Next = "-", Taxon = c("Fagaceae", "Salicaceae")
), "Two families of trees")
salicaceae <- keyFromLeads(data.frame(
  Statement = c("1", "1"), Choice = c("a", "b"),
  Character = c("Buds with one scale", "Buds with several scales"),
  Next = "-", Taxon = c("Salix", "Populus")
), "Genera of Salicaceae")
both <- mergeKeys(families, salicaceae, at = "Salicaceae")
both$leads
#>   Statement Choice                               Character Next    Taxon
#> 1         1      a                          Fruit an acorn    - Fagaceae
#> 2         1      b Fruit a capsule releasing cottony seeds    2         
#> 3         2      a                     Buds with one scale    -    Salix
#> 4         2      b                Buds with several scales    -  Populus
mergeKeys(families, salicaceae, at = "Salicaceae", labels = "prefix")$leads$Statement
#> [1] "1"            "1"            "Salicaceae.1" "Salicaceae.1"
